core.title: The documentation corpus renders with the reference renderer
core.given: The documentation corpus is being validated, whatever changed.
core.when: The documentation validator runs over the corpus.
core.then: The corpus MUST render with the stack's reference renderer, and an unresolvable internal reference in the corpus must be a validation failure; a build failure attributable to a specific document is FAIL.
prefer: Author documents that the reference renderer renders cleanly, and fix the document a render failure is attributed to
avoid: Feeding the render output tree back in as a render input
Scoring a crashed renderer, an unreadable tree or a missing toolchain as FAIL. Those are COULD_NOT_CHECK.
unless: The render output tree is generated OUTPUT and is never an input to the render
core.why: The reference renderer is chosen because an unresolvable internal reference must be a validation failure: only a real render exercises every internal reference, and a renderer that detects them weakly would let a broken corpus pass as clean.
evidence: The documentation validation report shows the reference renderer's build of the corpus completed with no build failure attributed to a document
verification: Verdict mapping: a build failure attributable to a specific document is FAIL. An absent toolchain, or a build failure not attributable to a specific document (a crashed renderer, an unreadable tree), is COULD_NOT_CHECK: never PASS and never FAIL.

An unresolvable internal reference must produce a validation failure (FAIL). How it surfaces is a realization choice — the renderer failing its build, or the validator promoting the renderer's diagnostics to FAIL — the obligation is on the validation outcome, not on the renderer's own build behavior. A renderer that detects unresolvable internal references weakly must not serve as the reference renderer.

Render inputs exclude the renderer's output tree. Documents that contain external links are still rendered; the links themselves are not fetched, because their liveness is a network property and checking it would make the gate non-deterministic.
Severity 1. Disposition strict: fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

No corpus directory or file extension is assumed: corpus discovery belongs to the validator, render output is never scanned as input, and the check's findings classify the verdict afterwards without gating activation.

fires: Every validation of the documentation corpus, including a clean one
A plan artifact or documentation change adds or edits a corpus document
A CI or toolchain change alters how the corpus is rendered, even though no document changed
doesNotFire: Files under the render output tree are not render inputs
Classifying a crashed renderer, an unreadable tree, a missing toolchain or any failure not pinned to a document: that verdict belongs to COULD_NOT_CHECK (the render obligation itself still applies)

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's reference renderer for the documentation corpus, with which the corpus must render; it must detect unresolvable internal references strongly enough that the check reports them as validation failures. Whether that happens through the renderer failing its own build or through diagnostics the validator promotes is a realization choice.
The tree the reference renderer writes its output to: generated output that is never a render input.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's reference renderer for the documentation corpus, with which the corpus must render; it must detect unresolvable internal references strongly enough that the check can report them as validation failures.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The tooling group covers languages, package manager, manifest, lockfiles, workspace declaration, test runner and URN resolver only; no key names the documentation renderer, and the idiom group describes source-level constructs, not documentation tooling. Without this key the core could not say which renderer a stack must render with.

proposedKeys.meaning: The tree the reference renderer writes its output to: generated output, never a render input.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roots.excluded is the single stack-wide never-scanned list of vendored and generated trees, and its doc explicitly reserves rule-scoped exclusions for the rule's own verification; no key names where render output is placed, which this rule needs to state 'output is never an input' per stack.

neutralityNotes: Two concrete facts had no vocabulary key and are proposed: the reference renderer (tooling.docs_renderer) and the render output tree (layout.render_output). The requirement on internal references is stated at the validation level: an unresolvable internal reference must be a validation failure, and whether that happens through the renderer failing its own build or through the validator promoting the renderer's diagnostics is left to each realization (in Bun, asciidoctor's document-attributable build failure is the mechanism). The profile constrains the renderer only to detect unresolvable internal references strongly enough for the check to report them, not to fail its own build. The corpus location is deliberately NOT a profile requirement because the Bun text assumes no directory or extension; corpus discovery belongs to the validator (stated in core verification). Realization-only identifiers stay Bun-only: the validator id 'docs_capability' (activation note, evidence, and the unnumbered audit.implementation.ref), the verdict id '.could-not-check' in activation.doesNotFire (neutralized to the generic COULD_NOT_CHECK), and the 'spec 2' citations. The Bun rule's 'Ruby runtime in CI' cost trade-off has no neutral equivalent and is recorded only in bunOnly.
